options: MongoDB Inc.'s official fully-managed cloud database service, available on AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure
A GUI tool for writing MongoDB queries
A separate NoSQL database unrelated to MongoDB
A MongoDB backup file format
questions.explain: Atlas is MongoDB's own managed service — it runs the same replica set and sharded cluster topologies covered in earlier lessons, but manages them for you.

questions.q: Which of the following does Atlas handle for you, compared to self-hosting?
options: Cluster provisioning, automated point-in-time backups, patching, and built-in monitoring/alerting
Nothing — Atlas is purely a hosting location with no operational management
Writing your application's queries for you
Choosing your data model so you don't have to design documents
questions.explain: Atlas automates the operational work a DBA would otherwise do by hand: provisioning, backups, patching, and monitoring.

questions.q: Per this lesson, when does self-hosting MongoDB still make sense over Atlas?
options: When an organization has strict data-residency requirements, existing on-prem investment, or highly specialized tuning needs
Self-hosting never makes sense anymore
Only when running MongoDB version 1.0
Atlas cannot run on Azure, only self-hosted MongoDB can
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as a real tradeoff, not Atlas being unconditionally better — some organizations have legitimate reasons to self-host.

questions.q: What is the Atlas M0 tier?
options: A free-forever shared cluster tier intended for learning and small projects
The most expensive dedicated production tier
A tier exclusive to sharded clusters
A deprecated tier no longer available
questions.explain: M0 is Atlas's free tier, used for learning and small-scale projects before moving to dedicated or serverless tiers.

questions.q: How does Atlas relate to Azure Cosmos DB's MongoDB API, per this lesson?
options: They're both legitimate but different ways to run MongoDB-compatible workloads — Atlas manages MongoDB itself, while Cosmos DB's MongoDB API puts a MongoDB driver interface on Azure's own distributed engine
They are the exact same product under a different name
Cosmos DB's MongoDB API is a feature built on top of Atlas
Atlas and Cosmos DB cannot both connect to MongoDB drivers
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes Atlas (MongoDB Inc.'s own managed service) from Cosmos DB's MongoDB API (Microsoft's engine speaking the MongoDB wire protocol) — both real, serving different needs.
